articles.title: Gold price prediction today: Will gold prices be range-bound? Check outlook for October 19, 2026 week
articles.summary: Gold price prediction today: Gold prices are seeing a range-bound bias, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research at Motilal Oswal Financial
articles.body: Gold price prediction today: Gold prices are seeing a range-bound bias, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. Let’s take a look at what the analyst has to say:Gold enters the week near Rs 148,000 after a sharp correction from the September high around Rs 163,000–165,000, with prices now consolidating after briefly falling towards the Rs 145,500–146,000 region.On the hourly chart, immediate structure remains weak to neutral, as gold is trading below the 20-period average near Rs 148,216, while the upper and lower Bollinger Bands are placed around Rs 148,832 and Rs 147,600 respectively.However, recent recovery from the Rs 145,500 area and subsequent consolidation around Rs 147,500–148,500 suggest that selling momentum is gradually stabilising. Immediate support is placed at Rs 147,500, followed by Rs 146,000–145,500; a sustained break below this region could expose Rs 143,500–144,000.On the upside, Rs 148,800–149,000 is the first hurdle, followed by the psychologically important Rs 150,000–150,500 zone. A sustained move above Rs 150,500 could improve momentum and open the way towards Rs 152,500–153,500, followed by Rs 155,000.From a broader one-to-three-month perspective, structure remains constructive as long as the Rs 145,000 region holds, with the current weakness still resembling a correction rather than a decisive reversal of the broader trend.Overall, the near-term bias remains range bound: Rs 150,500 on lower side, while a breakout above Rs 153,500 would provide stronger confirmation that the corrective phase is ending and could bring Rs 155,000–158,000 back into focus.Gold enters the week around $4,175 with a relatively resilient undertone as expectations of an immediate Federal Reserve rate hike have eased, although elevated real yields and a firm dollar continue to restrict the upside.Cautious commentary from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has reduced market expectations for an October increase to below 20%, providing some relief to bullion following the sharp repricing of rates during September.Softer crude oil prices have also moderated immediate energy-driven inflation concerns, although underlying price pressures continue to leave the possibility of another Fed hike later this year on the table. Importantly, gold has displayed unusual resilience despite substantially higher US Treasury yields.Investors increasingly appear to view elevated longer-term yields partly as compensation for rising US fiscal deficits, debt-servicing costs and concerns over debt sustainability, rather than simply as evidence of stronger economic growth.This has weakened the traditionally straightforward negative relationship between yields and bullion. Investment demand also remains supportive, with global gold ETF holdings increasing by around 187 tonnes during August and September, indicating continued strategic allocation despite recent price volatility.Chinese demand provides another underlying floor amid relatively low domestic interest rates and limited alternative investment opportunities, while central-bank purchases are estimated around 250–300 tonnes during Q3.Nevertheless, elevated real yields remain the principal near-term headwind. Attention now shifts towards the upcoming Fed meeting and PCE inflation, with softer inflation potentially supporting gold through lower rate expectations, while an upside surprise could revive tightening concerns and pressure bullion.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Festive rush puts two-wheelers in the fast lane, registrations jump 23%
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Two-wheelers have emerged as the strongest performers in India's festive vehicle market so far, with registrations climbing 23% year-on-year in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Two-wheelers have emerged as the strongest performers in India's festive vehicle market so far, with registrations climbing 23% year-on-year in the opening week of the season. Passenger vehicles also saw an increase, but their 7% growth was considerably lower, according to a Jefferies research report.The gap in performance comes even as both categories posted healthy registration growth in the first half of FY27. Between April and September, passenger vehicle registrations rose 28–29%, ahead of the 22% increase in two-wheelers. However, the latest festive-period figures show two-wheelers gaining pace despite a high base created by last year's Goods and Services Tax (GST) cuts.Jefferies assessed registrations between October 11 and 17, 2026, against September 22–28, 2025, to account for the shift in the festive calendar. In its equity research report, the brokerage said, "Auto registration data for the initial festive period shows strong demand momentum for 2Ws, trucks and tractors."Highlighting the performance of two-wheelers, it added, "2W registrations in the first 7 days of festive are up a strong 23% YoY, despite the high base post the GST cut last year,"Passenger vehicles recorded more modest gains during the same period. Jefferies noted, "PV registrations are also up 7% YoY, although lagging 2Ws on growth."The two-wheeler segment's performance also held up against a longer-term comparison. Over the past two years, registrations in the first festive week posted a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 17% compared with the corresponding period in 2024. Passenger vehicles recorded a lower CAGR of 10% over the same period. The comparison provides a longer-term measure of growth beyond the year-on-year increase.Trucks registered one of the sharpest increases among vehicle categories, with registrations nearly doubling to rise around 101% year-on-year in the first seven days of the festive season. However, the brokerage attributed part of this jump to a weak base, as truck registrations had fallen 32% during the corresponding period last year.Tractor registrations rose 28% year-on-year during the opening week of the festive season, exceeding the 18% growth recorded between April and September. Despite the stronger start, Jefferies flagged potential pressure on tractor demand in the second half of FY27, citing a high comparison base and weak monsoon conditions.The early figures point to growth across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, trucks and tractors, though the pace has varied between segments. Whether the initial momentum continues will become clearer as the festive period progresses, with the month-long season running through November 11.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
